_comment: Realm server for this host. uid_namespaces maps a Unix uid (a fleet owner) to the namespace(s) it may bind and send as.

policy._comment: Ordered rules, first match wins; no match -> default_allow. Deny by default and let strangers in through links and passports (spec 10.1). The {"links": true} entry marks where links are evaluated: rules before it override links, rules after it are fallbacks (spec Appendix B).

rules.note: everything else needs a link or a passport

links._comment: opt_out: endpoints beneath a namespace or realm side of a link may refuse it for themselves, and an endpoint may refuse every link a given key authorized (link revoke --key, spec 12.7). must_accept: links an endpoint may not revoke, opt out of or refuse by key, by the other side's address pattern or by a key that signed the link's passport (spec 12.8). auto_accept: endpoint patterns whose offers are accepted at once, through a passport like any accept (spec 12.9).

passports._comment: Site policy for passports (spec 12.8). host: the HTTPS host in passport URLs (default airc.<realm>). who: who may ask for a passport of each scope kind: agents (any client that may act for the scope), owner (the client whose namespaces contain the scope), admin (admin_uids only) or off. keys: keys entitled to authorize passports for a scope and everything beneath it (an endpoint's own published identity key is always entitled for itself and its sub-agents; key-add adds more, stored in passports.json). require: keys every passport whose scope matches the pattern must carry; when the key is site_key's, the server adds its signature itself. site_key: a file holding a 32-byte ed25519 seed (raw or base64), or the base64 seed; absent or "realm": the realm's own signing key; "none": no site key (then a client must sign every passport, including the one its server issues when it accepts a link offer, spec 12.9); entitled for the whole realm, and signs alone when a client sends no signature. present_from: which redeemers (realm names, address patterns, or *) may present passports of each kind; accept_from: from which issuing realms this server accepts grants of each kind. accept_require: keys a grant must carry for a matching local endpoint or namespace to accept it. redeem_as_namespace: whether local clients may redeem as one of their namespaces. delegate_who (agents|owner|admin|off, default owner) and delegate_to (realm patterns, default *): who may ask for a delegation and to which realms (spec 12.10). follow_forwards: root realms (patterns, default *) to which this server follows a knock forwarded with a delegated passport.

receipts._comment: Receipts (spec 6.7): whether this site's endpoints send seen/done receipts to senders that asked. default: senders in this realm; foreign: senders in other realms (off by default, a receipt shows when an agent's owner is active); scopes: per recipient endpoint or namespace (trailing /), the narrowest match winning. Values on | off | hook; hook POSTs {id, from, to, state, sender_realm, type} to the URL (3 s) and sends only on {"allow": true}.

http._comment: trusted_proxies: addresses or CIDR ranges of reverse proxies (nginx). When the direct peer is one, the client address (for the challenge send hook, spec 11.6) is the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry that is not itself a trusted proxy. Default loopback.

_comment_ttl: max_ttl: the longest message ttl accepted (seconds, default 7 days; longer is failed refused 'ttl too long'). clock_skew: added to it for how long message ids are remembered against replays (default 1 day, so 8 days). Spec 9.3, 7.3.
